Epic 253 - Water Page 2.0
<details> <summary> :rocket: User Story (Click to expand) </summary> **Main Objective** Provide users with a clear, flexible, and accurate view of their irrigation activities and water consumption through improved Water Insight cards, logging workflows, and settings, with integration capability for connected water meters. <details> <summary>User Stories (Click to expand)</summary> **Notifications** - As a user, I want to confirm irrigation with one click from notifications, so that my logs are always up to date. - As a user, I want to see a clear confirmation message when all logs are complete, so that I know there is nothing pending. **ET Card and Modal** - As a user, I want to see current ET, total since last irrigation, and forecast tomorrow, so that I can anticipate water needs. - As a user, I want to apply an ET correction factor, so that the displayed values match my local practices. - As a user, I want to compare ET values over 7, 30, 90 days or custom, so that I can spot longer-term patterns. **Rainfall Card and Modal** - As a user, I want to see rainfall today, since last irrigation, and forecast, so that I know how much natural water the field received. - As a user, I want to view rainfall as daily or cumulative over time ranges, so that I can compare with ET and irrigation. **Site Conditions** - As a user, I want to see soil and air conditions (temp, moisture), so that I understand field conditions when making irrigation decisions. **Water Usage Card and Modal** - As a user, I want to see water usage in the last 24h or last available reading, so that I know my consumption. - As a user, I want to see monthly totals with trend vs last month, so that I can track efficiency. - As a user with a connected meter, I want to see hourly usage for the last 3 days, so that I can monitor precise outflows. **Days Watered Card and Modal** - As a user, I want to see which days were irrigated on a calendar, so that I have a clear historical record. - As a user, I want to mark or unmark a day as irrigated, so that I can correct the log. - As a user, I want to plan irrigation days in advance, so that I can compare planned vs actual watering. **Total Water Use / Budget Card and Modal** - As a user, I want to see my total water use vs allowance, so that I know how much remains. - As a user, I want to compare usage to last year, so that I can measure savings or increases YTD. - As a user, I want to compare multiple years in monthly or cumulative views, so that I can track long-term trends. **Water Settings** - As a user, I want to set my irrigation period, so that notifications and logs apply only in that timeframe. - As a user, I want to set my irrigation schedule (daily, weekly, custom), so that notifications match my routine. - As a user, I want to enable or disable mobile notifications, so that I control reminders. - As a user, I want to set an annual allowance, so that the system can show progress and alert me when close to limits (alert part will be v2.0 not included in the current scope) **Water Records Table** - As a user, I want to see manual readings and connected meter readings in separate tabs, so that I can distinguish sources easily. - As a user, I want to filter and search water records (inflows and outflows), so that I can find specific data quickly. </details> **Scope** <details> <summary> :bell: :Top Left section - Daily Irrigation Notification and Logging (Click to expand) </summary> Help users confirm daily irrigation with a single click, and clearly show when all logs are complete. ### :dart: **Main Objective** The main goal is to **confirm whether irrigation actually happened**, and **collect the water usage or meter reading if it did**. This is not just a reminder — the confirmation step is essential. ### :white_check_mark: **How Notifications Work** * You will **receive one notification per outflow**, but **only if irrigation was planned** for that outflow based on the **Outflow Settings**. **Examples:** * If irrigation was planned only for **Outflow 1**, then **one notification** is sent. * If irrigation was planned for **Outflow 1, 2, and 3**, then the user will get **three notifications** — one for each outflow. ### :bell: **Notification Format** * **Message shown:** * Sunday, 4th January 2026\ Did you irrigate on this day?\ Outflow: Outflow 1 ![image.png](/uploads/7db4fdb58c27205cc7f80fbb2350feef/image.png){width="900" height="481"} ### :brain: **Notification Frequency Rules** * Notifications follow the schedule set in the **Outflow Settings**: * If frequency is **Tue/Thu**, prompts only appear on Tuesdays and Thursdays. * If set to **every other day**, prompts appear on alternating days based on the **start date**. ### :electric_plug: **Special Case – Connected (Metered) Outflows** * These still need a frequency setting (for internal tracking), * **but no prompts are shown** since irrigation is automatically tracked by the meter. ### :writing_hand: **Manual Logs Rule** * If the user **manually enters an irrigation record** for a given day and outflow, the system **removes the related prompt** for that day — no need to confirm again. ### :white_check_mark: **Inline Confirmation (No Modal)** * When the user clicks on the message, the message **expands inline** (no popup window). * The expanded section allows the user to **enter a value** (water consumption or meter reading). * **Entering a value is optional**, not mandatory. ![image.png](/uploads/e24c9605c44f95994ba776caccbe1943/image.png){width="311" height="439"} ### :package: **Bulk Confirmation** * Users can **select multiple days** (checkboxes) and **confirm irrigation in one action**. ![image.png](/uploads/78003ebe1120ca85b3972dcc0286880f/image.png){width="308" height="442"} If the user selects several messages across days, like: * Monday – Outflow 1 * Tuesday – Outflow 2 * Wednesday – Outflow 1 * Thursday – Outflow 2 * Friday – Outflow 1 Then: * The UI shows **one input field per outflow**. * If user enters **Outflow 1 = 150**, the system saves **50** each for Mon, Wed, and Fri. * If user enters **Outflow 2 = 100**, the system saves **50** each for Tue and Thu. ### ![image.png](/uploads/7dbb88fcd51fc0d51eaf91761c316844/image.png){width="429" height="600"} ### :brain: Smart Input Handling When the user expands a notification: * If there are **no future readings**, the input field is **pre-filled** with the last saved value. * If there are **readings after that date**, the input is left blank. * **Min/Max ranges** are shown to help guide valid entries. ### ### ![image.png](/uploads/68ac84608153999d315195b0b0e7d54f/image.png){width="312" height="435"} ### ### ### **Data Suggestions** * In **manual mode**: suggest the **last recorded volume**. * In **meter mode**: suggest the **next meter reading** using: * Last reading + last recorded delta * Example: 50,850 + 380 = **51,230** * :warning: **Guardrail**: * If the last reading is **older than 14 days**, leave the full reading field blank. similar UI like in the fleet reset counter ### ![image.png](/uploads/4efd978b623a840ec8ae0b1d3e94e3da/image.png){width="519" height="415"} ### :pushpin: **Special notes** When entering a **meter reading for a specific date**, the system must look at the readings **before and after** that date. If there is: * a reading **before** the selected date, and * a reading **after** the selected date, then the **calculated daily consumption for the earlier date must not be greater than the later reading**. **:mag: Meter Reading Validation & Guidance** * **Validations apply only to meter readings**, not to daily consumption entries. * If the system **cannot suggest a value** based on previous readings, it should still **guide the user**. * In such cases, the system must **display the minimum and maximum allowed values** for that range. ### :puzzle_piece: **Prompt Persistence Logic** * Notifications remain **visible for 7 days**. * If unanswered after 7 days, they are marked as **“unknown”**, ### :pushpin: **Additional Notes** * Prompts should only be sent on days that are **within the irrigation period** defined in the Water Settings. * Display notifications in **descending order by date** (most recent first). ### :arrows_counterclockwise: **Reading Validation Logic (Metered Outflows)** To avoid incorrect readings: * You can only enter a meter reading if it fits between the previous and next readings. **Example:** * Day 1: 500 * Day 6: 1000 * Day 8: 1200 * Day 10: 1500 * :white_check_mark: If user adds Day 4 = 700 → Valid (between 500 and 1000) **Invalid:** * :x: If user adds Day 4 = 1100 → Invalid (higher than next reading) * :x: If user adds Day 4 = 400 → Invalid (lower than previous reading) * In these cases, show a warning: * _“This reading doesn’t fit in the timeline. Please adjust readings.”_ ### :1234: Decimal Precision Rule * All the readings are displayed with **2 decimal places**. * Therefore, the **minimum allowed difference** between two consecutive meter readings must be **0.01**. </details> <details> <summary> :bar_chart: :Top Right Section - Enhanced Insight Cards (Click to expand) </summary> **Objective** Display clear, up-to-date water insights (ET, rainfall, water usage, days watered, and budget) in a set of dashboard cards to help users track irrigation activity, weather, and water usage trends in real time. ![Screenshot_2025-08-17_at_16.46.28](/uploads/b93cc2579b10a32fbfe0e55d9365f806/Screenshot_2025-08-17_at_16.46.28.png) ![Screenshot_2025-08-17_at_16.14.57](/uploads/17dbbcb4feddbf972700a856b656237c/Screenshot_2025-08-17_at_16.14.57.png) --- **:droplet: ET (Evapotranspiration)** **Purpose:** Shows daily ET to help users estimate water loss from turf. **Fields to show:** - **ET last 24h →** Display value in mm. - **Total since last irrigation →** Show value + number of days. - **ET tomorrow →** Forecasted ET value. - **Adjusted ET →** If the Correction Factor in Settings ≠ 100%, show adjusted ET next to the value. **Calculation logic:** Adjusted ET = Reference ET × Correction Factor (e.g., 5.2mm × 0.85 = 4.4mm) --- **:cloud_rain: Rainfall** **Purpose:** Displays rainfall data for better irrigation planning. **Fields to show:** - **Rainfall last 24h →** mm value. - **Rainfall since last irrigation →** mm value. - **Rainfall +24 hour forecast →** Show value and probability (e.g., 5mm (50%)). --- **:round_pushpin: Site Conditions** **Purpose:** Give context about turf environment. **Fields to show:** - **Air Temperature →** Now, Min, Max (e.g., 15°C | 14°C – 18°C). - **Soil Temperature →** Now, Min, Max. - **Soil Moisture →** Now, Min, Max. **Display colors** - Now - (Black) - Min - (Blue) - Max - (Red) --- **:shower: Water Usage (Outflows)** **Purpose:** Tracks water usage trends and alerts users of increases/decreases. **Fields to show:** - **Water usage last 24h →** Show total (e.g., 2,495 m³) (23%). - Example: 2,495 m³ (23%) means 2,495 m³ is 23% of the total monthly forecast - **If data is missing →** Fallback to the most recent available reading and show how many days ago it was recorded (e.g., Last reading: 4 days ago). - **Total this month →** Show cumulative water usage for the current month (e.g., 10,852 m³) along with the trend compared to last month (e.g., ↑ 12%). - **Forecast used this month →** Show the expected or forecasted water usage value for the month (e.g., 18,028 m³). (If not available yet, display placeholder “Coming soon”). **Trend Display:** - (\> 0%) Upward = Red Arrow "↑" - (\< 0%) Downward = Green Arrow "↓" - (= 0%) Neutral = Grey dash "-" --- **:seedling: Days Watered** **Purpose:** Helps monitor watering activity across the month and year. **Fields to show:** - Days watered this month (e.g., 12 days). - Total days watered this year (e.g., 110 days). - Average water/day this month + % trend vs. last month. **Trend Display:** - (\> 0%) Upward = Red Arrow "↑" - (\< 0%) Downward = Green Arrow "↓" - (= 0%) Neutral = Grey dash "-" --- **:chart_with_upwards_trend: Total Water Use / Budget** **Purpose:** Tracks water consumption progress against annual target. **Fields to show:** - **Total this year vs. allowance →** Pull from Water Settings (e.g., 45,498 m³ / 75,000 m³). - **Visual progress bar →** Fill percentage = total used / allowance. (% next to it) - Progress bar color rules: - Use gray if usage is below 60% of the yearly limit. - Use yellow if usage is between 60% and 80%. - Use red if usage is over 80%. - **vs. Last year →** Value + difference (YTD comparison), shown in green for surplus. - If current usage is less than last year, show the saved amount in green → e.g., 1,712 m³ Saved. - If current usage is more than last year, show the overused amount in red → e.g., 1,712 m³ Overused. --- </details> <details> <summary> :newspaper: :Card Modals (Click to expand) </summary> <details> <summary> :bar_chart: Water Usage Card Modal (Inflows / Outflows) </summary> **Objective:** Allow users to view detailed water usage data through modal popups launched from the Water Usage insight card. The modal should support time filtering, multiple view types (daily, cumulative, hourly), and pump-based breakdowns. ![Screenshot_2025-08-17_at_16.02.16](/uploads/24016ef2bbbc0dcca5eee796677a6b46/Screenshot_2025-08-17_at_16.02.16.png){width="826" height="298"} :puzzle_piece: **Modal Activation** - Clicking on the Water Usage card (Outflow or Inflow) opens a graph modal. - The modal includes: - Graph with bars - Time filter - Pump selector - View toggle (Daily, Cumulative, and Hourly if available) --- :repeat: **Tabs: Inflows and Outflows** - Modal must have a tab switcher at the top: - Outflows (default active tab) - Inflows - The graph must update based on selected tab data (e.g., pump, date). --- :date: **Range Selector (Time Filters)** - Dropdown menu to select a time range: - Last 14 days (default) - Last 30 days - Last 90 days - Custom (date picker) - Selection controls how many bars appear in the graph: - 14-day range → 14 bars - 30-day range → 30 bars - 90-day range → 90 bars --- :gear: **Type Toggle (Graph Style)** Toggle group with these options: - Daily (should be the correct label instead of “Monthly”) - Cumulative - Hourly (only shown if connected water meter exists) **View behavior:** - Daily (default): - Each bar = total usage per day. - If multiple pumps are selected, stack bars per pump using different colors. - Cumulative: - Each bar = running total up to that day (Day 1 = 100, Day 2 = 230, etc.) - If multiple pumps are selected, stack bars per pump using different colors. - Hourly (connected meter only): - Each bar = total water used per hour. - Default range = last 3 days. --- ### :bulb: Mixed Outflows (Hourly vs. Non-Hourly) If the user selects a mix of connected (Shayp) and normal outflows: (Pump 1 connected, Pump 2 and 3 Normal) - Show a **validation message** such as - “Hourly data not available for Pump 2 and Pump 3.” - Only show hourly data for **connected (Shayp)** outflows. --- :droplet: **Pump Selector** - Multi-select checkboxes for available sources: - Pump 1, Pump 2, Pump 3, etc. - Selected pumps are reflected in the graph - **Connected meters** should display a small **Wi-Fi or link icon** next to their name to indicate they are linked to a Shayp device. --- :pushpin: **Tooltip & UI Behaviors** - Tooltips must appear when the user hovers over bars: - Show exact value, date, and pump breakdown. - Modal layout must be responsive across screen sizes. --- :brain: **Developer Notes** - Replace label “Monthly” with “Daily” - Graph should re-render instantly when: - Range, tab, type, or pump filters are changed. - “Hourly” type should only appear if the connected water meter (Shayp) is active for that site. --- </details> <details> <summary> :date: Days Watered Card Modal (Irrigation Events Calendar) </summary> **Objective:** Let users view, confirm, and manage past irrigation events using a visual calendar. It should also display planned irrigation days based on user settings. ![image.png](/uploads/7c83b10be0e20bfa3fac527a287e2512/image.png){width="900" height="562"} :unlock: **Access & Activation** - When the user clicks on the "Days Watered" card on the Water Insight dashboard: - Open a modal calendar view for the current month. - Display irrigation status using colored dots for each day. - When multiple outflows exist, an **Outflow Picker** should appear in the modal for the user to select outflow(s). --- :art: **Calendar Dot Legend** This color system helps users quickly understand the irrigation status for each day and each outflow on the calendar. **Color Meaning** * :green_circle: **Green** → Irrigation was confirmed by a **manual entry** (actual water record). * :large_blue_circle: **Blue** → User confirmed irrigation via **notification**, but no actual water record is found. * :red_circle: **Red** → User confirmed **“No irrigation”** via notification. * :large_blue_diamond: **Light Blue** → **Planned irrigation** day (based on Water Settings), but no confirmation or record yet. - No dot → No data provided / unknown status. Hovering over any watered date shows the total water usage (outflow) for that day. * Calendar click cycle (explicit): * Light blue (Planned irrigation) → Blue (confirmed irrigation via notification) → Red (no irrigation) → Light blue (Planned irrigation). * Outflow picker must be visible in the modal for clarity when multiple outflows exist. ### ### :brain: **Important Rule** If there is already a **manual irrigation record** for that day and outflow, the user **cannot change the status** from the calendar. This avoids conflicts between real records and user interactions. ### ### :round_pushpin:**When “All” Outflows Are Selected** If the user views the calendar in **"All outflows" mode**, use the following logic to decide what dot color to show: * :green_circle: Show **Green** → If **at least one outflow** has an actual irrigation record * :large_blue_circle: Show **Blue** → If **no manual records**, but **at least one outflow** was confirmed via notification * :red_circle: Show **Red** → If **no irrigation was confirmed** on any outflow * :large_blue_circle: + :red_circle: = :large_blue_circle: (If some are confirmed, some are not → treat as confirmed) * :large_blue_circle: + :large_blue_diamond: = :large_blue_circle: (If some are confirmed via notification, others are just planned → treat as confirmed) * :red_circle: + :large_blue_diamond: = :large_blue_diamond: (If some are marked as “no”, others are just planned → treat as planned) ### ### :mouse_three_button: **Clickable Status with “All” Outflows** If the user clicks on a date while in **“All” outflows view**: * Open a **side modal** that lets the user adjust the irrigation status **for each outflow individually**. * This ensures they can refine the data instead of applying one status to all. --- :brain: **Planned Irrigation Days Logic** - Based on the “Default Irrigation Frequency” selected in Water Settings: - Daily - Every other day - Specific weekdays (e.g., Mon/Wed/Fri) - Once per week (select a day) - System should automatically highlight past planned dates (not future ones) in light blue. :warning: Do not display planned irrigation for future dates. --- :tools: **Developer Notes** - Calendar shows the current month by default, but allow navigation to past months. - Total number of irrigated days (confirmed green) is calculated and displayed at the top. - Make sure red, blue, and light blue dots are visually distinct and accessible. --- </details> <details> <summary> :droplet: Water Budget Card Modal (Total Water Use) </summary> **Objective:** Allow users to explore historical total water usage (outflows) across a full calendar year, compare usage by pump, switch between monthly and cumulative trends, and optionally compare multiple years. ![Screenshot_2025-08-17_at_16.03.18](/uploads/b3980e2880a35014d657faf3d7b3b936/Screenshot_2025-08-17_at_16.03.18.png) :calendar: **Access & Activation** - Clicking on the “Total Water Use / Budget” card on the dashboard opens a modal containing a full-year line chart. - The default view shows the current year, broken down by month. --- :chart_with_upwards_trend: **Graph Design & Display** - X-axis: Month of the year (Jan–Dec) - Y-axis: Total water usage (in m³) - Tooltip on Hover: Display total usage for the selected month + breakdown by pump (if multiple are selected). - Graph type: - Line graph (one or more lines depending on selected years/pumps) --- :wrench: **Filter Controls** **Year Selector** - Dropdown to select year(s) for comparison. - Allow multi-year comparison: overlay multiple lines for different years (e.g., 2024 vs 2025). **Outflow (Pump) Selector** - Multi-select checkboxes: Pump 1, Pump 2, Pump 3 - Users can toggle any combination of pumps to isolate usage by source. **View Type** - Monthly (default): Each point shows usage for that month only. - Cumulative: Each point shows running total from Jan to that month (e.g., Feb = Jan + Feb total). --- :brain: **Developer Notes** - The data source should be consistent with water outflow logs (manual + connected meters). - Display unit: m³ - Ensure graphs are responsive and color-coded for multi-year comparison. - Label each line clearly when multi-year comparison is active (e.g., “2024”, “2025”). - Cumulative logic: keep running sum for each month per selected year and pump combination. --- </details> <details> <summary> :white_sun_rain_cloud: ET & Rainfall Card Modals </summary> **Objective:** Allow users to view detailed historical data for Evapotranspiration (ET) and Rainfall through modals launched from the Water Insight dashboard. Charts should support different timeframes and display either daily or cumulative values. ![Screenshot_2025-08-17_at_16.07.15](/uploads/33a98c8b9937e851f2878dbd960603ae/Screenshot_2025-08-17_at_16.07.15.png) :pushpin: **Modal Access** - Clicking on the ET or Rainfall card opens a dedicated modal. - Each modal contains a visual graph and time filters. --- :chart_with_upwards_trend: **Graph filters for both ET and Rainfall** - Time Filters (Range): - Last 7 days (default) - Last 30 days - Last 90 days - Custom (date picker) - View Options (Type): - Daily → Each point/bar represents individual day value. - Cumulative → Each point shows the running total. - Tooltip on hover: - Show date + value (mm) - For ET: also show Adjusted ET if applicable (only in ET graph) - Graph type: Line or bar chart (whichever fits design system) --- :thermometer: **ET Modal (Evapotranspiration)** - Data to display: - ET₀ (reference value from weather station) - Adjusted ET (ET₀ × correction factor) - If correction factor ≠ 100%, display both ET₀ and Adjusted ET in the tooltip and legend. - Unit: mm per day --- :cloud_rain: **Rainfall Modal** - Data to display: - Daily rainfall - Rainfall forecast (if available) - Only show actual rainfall data for now (no forecast needed at this stage). - Unit: mm per day --- :wrench: **Developer Notes** - Graph must update dynamically when users change: - Date range - View type (daily/cumulative) - Default State: - ET modal: Show last 7 days, daily view - Rainfall modal: Show last 7 days, daily view --- </details> </details> <details> <summary> :gear: Water Settings Configuration Panel (Click to expand) </summary> **Objective:** Allow users to set irrigation-related preferences such as water allowance, irrigation period, correction factor, and app notifications. These settings control how data is calculated and displayed across the Water Insight dashboard. ![image](/uploads/def1c30060eb93ce4b8720f5c3a41bde/image.png){width="813" height="343"} --- ![image](/uploads/0102cd66572a282ec49fa3172b15d74d/image.png){width="845" height="564"} --- ## ![image](/uploads/5ba43e0aa1555dca4aadc97146eb9661/image.png){width="966" height="544"} :receipt: **Fields & Functional Requirements** **Annual Water Allowance (Target)** - Users can enter a target water usage amount for the year (e.g., 75,000 m³). - This target is set per outflow/pump level, not tenant-wise. - Value is used in the Water Budget card to calculate progress and % used. - **Note:** The total water budget card is the sum of all outflow allowances. --- **Irrigation Period (From / To)** - Users define the active irrigation period during the year (e.g., March to November). This period: - Controls when daily irrigation notifications are triggered. - Filters data in ET, rainfall, days watered dashboards. - :warning: If the user changes the period mid-season (May to November), the system: - Preserves historical logs from outside the new date range. - Shows a warning: “Some data exists outside the selected irrigation period.” --- **Default Irrigation Frequency** - Drop-down to select how often irrigation typically happens: - Daily - Every other day - Once per week (select day) - Specific weekdays (multi-select: e.g., Mon, Wed, Fri) --- **Mobile App Notifications** - Toggle: Enabled / Disabled - If Enabled: - Sends daily push prompt to mobile app: - "Did you irrigate yesterday evening?" - (User can answer Yes :white_check_mark: or No :x:). - Default is Enabled on first setup. --- **Target ET / ET Correction Factor (%)** - A numeric field (default = 100%) that lets users adjust the ET used in calculations. - How it works: - Reference ET₀ comes from a weather station (e.g., 5.2 mm). - If Correction Factor = 85%, then Adjusted ET = 5.2 × 0.85 = 4.4 mm. - Display Logic: - If value ≠ 100%, both ET₀ and Adjusted ET must be shown in: - Insight Cards - ET Modals / Graphs --- **Default Values that should load for the water settings per outflow** - ET factor = 1 (100%) (no adjustment). - Mobile App notifications = Enabled. - Add field for “Preferred reminder time”. Default = 3 pm site-local time (important for multi-country tenants). - Annual Allowance = 0 (neutral until set). - Irrigation Period = Jan–Dec (neutral default, as periods differ worldwide). - Irrigation Frequency = Weekly (default = Wednesday, to avoid overwhelming with daily prompts). </details> <details> <summary> :electric_plug: :Connected Water Meter Integration (Shayp v1.0) (Click to expand) </summary> **Objective:** Integrate IoT-connected water meters into the Water Insight system to capture hourly/daily flow data, display usage summaries, and distinguish between manual and automated sources. :briefcase: **Key Functionalities** **Device Linking (Backend Only)** - Device linking will be handled internally by our development team (no UI at this stage). - Devices will be mapped in the backend via database or config setup. - For now, coordinate with (Sasitha, Tharuka) for device setup and data structure alignment. --- **Data Storage – New Table** - Create a new database table to store hourly inflow/outflow readings from Shayp devices. - Table structure should support: - Device ID / Source - Timestamp - Flow Direction (Inflow / Outflow) - Volume (m³) --- **Daily Totals Calculation** - The system should automatically compute daily totals based on the hourly inflow/outflow records. - These totals will be displayed in the Water Insight card. --- **Toggle: Hourly / Daily / Cumulative View** - Add a radio button toggle in the UI (total usage section or modal) with 3 options: - Hourly - Daily - Cumulative - When users switch between these views: - The corresponding graph or data table should update accordingly. - Use consistent units (m³) and color schemes for all views. --- **Source Indicator (Manual vs. Automated)** - Clearly show whether a reading is: - Manual (entered by user) - Automated (from IoT device) - Even if a site has connected meters, some readings may still be manual (e.g., if a specific source isn't linked to a device yet). </details> <details> <summary> :clipboard: :Bottom Section - Water Usage Records Table (Click to expand) </summary> :bangbang: **:Wireframe here is not perfectly filled, PLEASE make sure to consider description** **Objective:** Provide users with a detailed, filterable table of water usage entries—both manual and from connected meters—to view, edit, or delete records as needed. ![Screenshot_2025-08-17_at_16.02.08](/uploads/8b780d54d77f28993fdba1fe9a4da47c/Screenshot_2025-08-17_at_16.02.08.png) **Water Records Table** ![image](/uploads/8b4f6d5e03cfba6eef492e2d3b66ae4e/image.png){width="902" height="410"} **Main Features** **Tabs** - Two tabs to switch between: - Manual Readings (entered by user) - Connected Meter Logs (auto-synced device data) --- **Table Columns** - **Date →** The date of the recorded usage - **Water Flow →** Pump name (e.g., Pump 1, Pump 2) - **Measurement →** Value + unit (e.g., 50500 m³) - Show an icon indicating source: - :droplet: = daily consumption - :pager: = meter readings - **Comments →** Optional user-entered notes (e.g., “Strong drought”, “Tournament mid-day watering”) - Epic 253 - Water Page 2.0

    •
  • View options
    • Open created 9 months ago by Valentine Godin

    🚀 User Story (Click to expand)

    Main Objective

    Provide users with a clear, flexible, and accurate view of their irrigation activities and water consumption through improved Water Insight cards, logging workflows, and settings, with integration capability for connected water meters.

    User Stories (Click to expand)

    Notifications

    • As a user, I want to confirm irrigation with one click from notifications, so that my logs are always up to date.
    • As a user, I want to see a clear confirmation message when all logs are complete, so that I know there is nothing pending.

    ET Card and Modal

    • As a user, I want to see current ET, total since last irrigation, and forecast tomorrow, so that I can anticipate water needs.
    • As a user, I want to apply an ET correction factor, so that the displayed values match my local practices.
    • As a user, I want to compare ET values over 7, 30, 90 days or custom, so that I can spot longer-term patterns.

    Rainfall Card and Modal

    • As a user, I want to see rainfall today, since last irrigation, and forecast, so that I know how much natural water the field received.
    • As a user, I want to view rainfall as daily or cumulative over time ranges, so that I can compare with ET and irrigation.

    Site Conditions

    • As a user, I want to see soil and air conditions (temp, moisture), so that I understand field conditions when making irrigation decisions.

    Water Usage Card and Modal

    • As a user, I want to see water usage in the last 24h or last available reading, so that I know my consumption.
    • As a user, I want to see monthly totals with trend vs last month, so that I can track efficiency.
    • As a user with a connected meter, I want to see hourly usage for the last 3 days, so that I can monitor precise outflows.

    Days Watered Card and Modal

    • As a user, I want to see which days were irrigated on a calendar, so that I have a clear historical record.
    • As a user, I want to mark or unmark a day as irrigated, so that I can correct the log.
    • As a user, I want to plan irrigation days in advance, so that I can compare planned vs actual watering.

    Total Water Use / Budget Card and Modal

    • As a user, I want to see my total water use vs allowance, so that I know how much remains.
    • As a user, I want to compare usage to last year, so that I can measure savings or increases YTD.
    • As a user, I want to compare multiple years in monthly or cumulative views, so that I can track long-term trends.

    Water Settings

    • As a user, I want to set my irrigation period, so that notifications and logs apply only in that timeframe.
    • As a user, I want to set my irrigation schedule (daily, weekly, custom), so that notifications match my routine.
    • As a user, I want to enable or disable mobile notifications, so that I control reminders.
    • As a user, I want to set an annual allowance, so that the system can show progress and alert me when close to limits (alert part will be v2.0 not included in the current scope)

    Water Records Table

    • As a user, I want to see manual readings and connected meter readings in separate tabs, so that I can distinguish sources easily.
    • As a user, I want to filter and search water records (inflows and outflows), so that I can find specific data quickly.

    Scope

    🔔 :Top Left section - Daily Irrigation Notification and Logging (Click to expand)

     Help users confirm daily irrigation with a single click, and clearly show when all logs are complete.

    🎯 Main Objective

    The main goal is to confirm whether irrigation actually happened, and collect the water usage or meter reading if it did. This is not just a reminder — the confirmation step is essential.

    ✅ How Notifications Work

    • You will receive one notification per outflow, but only if irrigation was planned for that outflow based on the Outflow Settings.

    Examples:

    • If irrigation was planned only for Outflow 1, then one notification is sent.
    • If irrigation was planned for Outflow 1, 2, and 3, then the user will get three notifications — one for each outflow.

    🔔 Notification Format

    • Message shown:
    • Sunday, 4th January 2026
      Did you irrigate on this day?
      Outflow: Outflow 1

    🧠 Notification Frequency Rules

    • Notifications follow the schedule set in the Outflow Settings:
      • If frequency is Tue/Thu, prompts only appear on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
      • If set to every other day, prompts appear on alternating days based on the start date.

    🔌 Special Case – Connected (Metered) Outflows

    • These still need a frequency setting (for internal tracking),
    • but no prompts are shown since irrigation is automatically tracked by the meter.

    ✍️ Manual Logs Rule

    • If the user manually enters an irrigation record for a given day and outflow, the system removes the related prompt for that day — no need to confirm again.

    ✅ Inline Confirmation (No Modal)

    • When the user clicks on the message, the message expands inline (no popup window).
    • The expanded section allows the user to enter a value (water consumption or meter reading).
    • Entering a value is optional, not mandatory.

    📦 Bulk Confirmation

    • Users can select multiple days (checkboxes) and confirm irrigation in one action.

    If the user selects several messages across days, like:

    • Monday – Outflow 1
    • Tuesday – Outflow 2
    • Wednesday – Outflow 1
    • Thursday – Outflow 2
    • Friday – Outflow 1

    Then:

    • The UI shows one input field per outflow.
    • If user enters Outflow 1 = 150, the system saves 50 each for Mon, Wed, and Fri.
    • If user enters Outflow 2 = 100, the system saves 50 each for Tue and Thu.

    🧠 Smart Input Handling

    When the user expands a notification:

    • If there are no future readings, the input field is pre-filled with the last saved value.
    • If there are readings after that date, the input is left blank.
    • Min/Max ranges are shown to help guide valid entries.

    Data Suggestions

    • In manual mode: suggest the last recorded volume.
    • In meter mode: suggest the next meter reading using:
      • Last reading + last recorded delta
      • Example: 50,850 + 380 = 51,230
    • ⚠️ Guardrail:
    • If the last reading is older than 14 days, leave the full reading field blank.

    similar UI like in the fleet reset counter

    📌 Special notes

    When entering a meter reading for a specific date, the system must look at the readings before and after that date.

    If there is:

    • a reading before the selected date, and
    • a reading after the selected date,

    then the calculated daily consumption for the earlier date must not be greater than the later reading.

    🔍 Meter Reading Validation & Guidance

    • Validations apply only to meter readings, not to daily consumption entries.
    • If the system cannot suggest a value based on previous readings, it should still guide the user.
    • In such cases, the system must display the minimum and maximum allowed values for that range.

    🧩 Prompt Persistence Logic

    • Notifications remain visible for 7 days.
    • If unanswered after 7 days, they are marked as “unknown”,

    📌 Additional Notes

    • Prompts should only be sent on days that are within the irrigation period defined in the Water Settings.
    • Display notifications in descending order by date (most recent first).

    🔄 Reading Validation Logic (Metered Outflows)

    To avoid incorrect readings:

    • You can only enter a meter reading if it fits between the previous and next readings.

    Example:

    • Day 1: 500
    • Day 6: 1000
    • Day 8: 1200
    • Day 10: 1500
    • ✅ If user adds Day 4 = 700 → Valid (between 500 and 1000)

    Invalid:

    • ❌ If user adds Day 4 = 1100 → Invalid (higher than next reading)
    • ❌ If user adds Day 4 = 400 → Invalid (lower than previous reading)
    • In these cases, show a warning:
    • “This reading doesn’t fit in the timeline. Please adjust readings.”

    🔢 Decimal Precision Rule

    • All the readings are displayed with 2 decimal places.
    • Therefore, the minimum allowed difference between two consecutive meter readings must be 0.01.

    📊 :Top Right Section - Enhanced Insight Cards (Click to expand)

    Objective

    Display clear, up-to-date water insights (ET, rainfall, water usage, days watered, and budget) in a set of dashboard cards to help users track irrigation activity, weather, and water usage trends in real time.

    💧 ET (Evapotranspiration)

    Purpose: Shows daily ET to help users estimate water loss from turf.

    Fields to show:

    • ET last 24h → Display value in mm.
    • Total since last irrigation → Show value + number of days.
    • ET tomorrow → Forecasted ET value.
    • Adjusted ET → If the Correction Factor in Settings ≠ 100%, show adjusted ET next to the value.

    Calculation logic:

    Adjusted ET = Reference ET × Correction Factor (e.g., 5.2mm × 0.85 = 4.4mm)

    🌧️ Rainfall

    Purpose: Displays rainfall data for better irrigation planning.

    Fields to show:

    • Rainfall last 24h → mm value.
    • Rainfall since last irrigation → mm value.
    • Rainfall +24 hour forecast → Show value and probability (e.g., 5mm (50%)).

    📍 Site Conditions

    Purpose: Give context about turf environment.

    Fields to show:

    • Air Temperature → Now, Min, Max (e.g., 15°C | 14°C – 18°C).
    • Soil Temperature → Now, Min, Max.
    • Soil Moisture → Now, Min, Max.

    Display colors

    • Now - (Black)
    • Min - (Blue)
    • Max - (Red)

    🚿 Water Usage (Outflows)

    Purpose: Tracks water usage trends and alerts users of increases/decreases.

    Fields to show:

    • Water usage last 24h → Show total (e.g., 2,495 m³) (23%).
      • Example: 2,495 m³ (23%) means 2,495 m³ is 23% of the total monthly forecast
    • If data is missing → Fallback to the most recent available reading and show how many days ago it was recorded (e.g., Last reading: 4 days ago).
    • Total this month → Show cumulative water usage for the current month (e.g., 10,852 m³) along with the trend compared to last month (e.g., ↑ 12%).
    • Forecast used this month → Show the expected or forecasted water usage value for the month (e.g., 18,028 m³). (If not available yet, display placeholder “Coming soon”).

    Trend Display:

    • (> 0%) Upward = Red Arrow "↑"
    • (< 0%) Downward = Green Arrow "↓"
    • (= 0%) Neutral = Grey dash "-"

    🌱 Days Watered

    Purpose: Helps monitor watering activity across the month and year.

    Fields to show:

    • Days watered this month (e.g., 12 days).
    • Total days watered this year (e.g., 110 days).
    • Average water/day this month + % trend vs. last month.

    Trend Display:

    • (> 0%) Upward = Red Arrow "↑"
    • (< 0%) Downward = Green Arrow "↓"
    • (= 0%) Neutral = Grey dash "-"

    📈 Total Water Use / Budget

    Purpose: Tracks water consumption progress against annual target.

    Fields to show:

    • Total this year vs. allowance → Pull from Water Settings (e.g., 45,498 m³ / 75,000 m³).
    • Visual progress bar → Fill percentage = total used / allowance. (% next to it)
    • Progress bar color rules:
      • Use gray if usage is below 60% of the yearly limit.
      • Use yellow if usage is between 60% and 80%.
      • Use red if usage is over 80%.
    • vs. Last year → Value + difference (YTD comparison), shown in green for surplus.
      • If current usage is less than last year, show the saved amount in green → e.g., 1,712 m³ Saved.
      • If current usage is more than last year, show the overused amount in red → e.g., 1,712 m³ Overused.

    📰 :Card Modals (Click to expand)

    📊 Water Usage Card Modal (Inflows / Outflows)

    Objective:

    Allow users to view detailed water usage data through modal popups launched from the Water Usage insight card. The modal should support time filtering, multiple view types (daily, cumulative, hourly), and pump-based breakdowns.

    🧩 Modal Activation

    • Clicking on the Water Usage card (Outflow or Inflow) opens a graph modal.
    • The modal includes:
      • Graph with bars
      • Time filter
      • Pump selector
      • View toggle (Daily, Cumulative, and Hourly if available)

    🔁 Tabs: Inflows and Outflows

    • Modal must have a tab switcher at the top:
      • Outflows (default active tab)
      • Inflows
    • The graph must update based on selected tab data (e.g., pump, date).

    📅 Range Selector (Time Filters)

    • Dropdown menu to select a time range:
      • Last 14 days (default)
      • Last 30 days
      • Last 90 days
      • Custom (date picker)
    • Selection controls how many bars appear in the graph:
      • 14-day range → 14 bars
      • 30-day range → 30 bars
      • 90-day range → 90 bars

    ⚙️ Type Toggle (Graph Style)

    Toggle group with these options:

    • Daily (should be the correct label instead of “Monthly”)
    • Cumulative
    • Hourly (only shown if connected water meter exists)

    View behavior:

    • Daily (default):
      • Each bar = total usage per day.
      • If multiple pumps are selected, stack bars per pump using different colors.
    • Cumulative:
      • Each bar = running total up to that day (Day 1 = 100, Day 2 = 230, etc.)
      • If multiple pumps are selected, stack bars per pump using different colors.
    • Hourly (connected meter only):
      • Each bar = total water used per hour.
      • Default range = last 3 days.

    💡 Mixed Outflows (Hourly vs. Non-Hourly)

    If the user selects a mix of connected (Shayp) and normal outflows: (Pump 1 connected, Pump 2 and 3 Normal)

    • Show a validation message such as
      • “Hourly data not available for Pump 2 and Pump 3.”
    • Only show hourly data for connected (Shayp) outflows.

    💧 Pump Selector

    • Multi-select checkboxes for available sources:
      • Pump 1, Pump 2, Pump 3, etc.
    • Selected pumps are reflected in the graph
    • Connected meters should display a small Wi-Fi or link icon next to their name to indicate they are linked to a Shayp device.

    📌 Tooltip & UI Behaviors

    • Tooltips must appear when the user hovers over bars:
      • Show exact value, date, and pump breakdown.
    • Modal layout must be responsive across screen sizes.

    🧠 Developer Notes

    • Replace label “Monthly” with “Daily”
    • Graph should re-render instantly when:
      • Range, tab, type, or pump filters are changed.
    • “Hourly” type should only appear if the connected water meter (Shayp) is active for that site.

    📅 Days Watered Card Modal (Irrigation Events Calendar)

    Objective:

    Let users view, confirm, and manage past irrigation events using a visual calendar. It should also display planned irrigation days based on user settings.

    🔓 Access & Activation

    • When the user clicks on the "Days Watered" card on the Water Insight dashboard:
      • Open a modal calendar view for the current month.
      • Display irrigation status using colored dots for each day.
      • When multiple outflows exist, an Outflow Picker should appear in the modal for the user to select outflow(s).

    🎨 Calendar Dot Legend

    This color system helps users quickly understand the irrigation status for each day and each outflow on the calendar.

    Color Meaning

    • 🟢 Green → Irrigation was confirmed by a manual entry (actual water record).
    • 🔵 Blue → User confirmed irrigation via notification, but no actual water record is found.
    • 🔴 Red → User confirmed “No irrigation” via notification.
    • 🔷 Light Blue → Planned irrigation day (based on Water Settings), but no confirmation or record yet.
    • No dot → No data provided / unknown status.

    Hovering over any watered date shows the total water usage (outflow) for that day.

    • Calendar click cycle (explicit):
      • Light blue (Planned irrigation) → Blue (confirmed irrigation via notification) → Red (no irrigation) → Light blue (Planned irrigation).
      • Outflow picker must be visible in the modal for clarity when multiple outflows exist.

    🧠 Important Rule

    If there is already a manual irrigation record for that day and outflow, the user cannot change the status from the calendar. This avoids conflicts between real records and user interactions.

    📍When “All” Outflows Are Selected

    If the user views the calendar in "All outflows" mode, use the following logic to decide what dot color to show:

    • 🟢 Show Green → If at least one outflow has an actual irrigation record
    • 🔵 Show Blue → If no manual records, but at least one outflow was confirmed via notification
    • 🔴 Show Red → If no irrigation was confirmed on any outflow
    • 🔵 + 🔴 = 🔵 (If some are confirmed, some are not → treat as confirmed)
    • 🔵 + 🔷 = 🔵 (If some are confirmed via notification, others are just planned → treat as confirmed)
    • 🔴 + 🔷 = 🔷 (If some are marked as “no”, others are just planned → treat as planned)

    🖱️ Clickable Status with “All” Outflows

    If the user clicks on a date while in “All” outflows view:

    • Open a side modal that lets the user adjust the irrigation status for each outflow individually.
    • This ensures they can refine the data instead of applying one status to all.

    🧠 Planned Irrigation Days Logic

    • Based on the “Default Irrigation Frequency” selected in Water Settings:
      • Daily
      • Every other day
      • Specific weekdays (e.g., Mon/Wed/Fri)
      • Once per week (select a day)
    • System should automatically highlight past planned dates (not future ones) in light blue.

    ⚠️ Do not display planned irrigation for future dates.

    🛠️ Developer Notes

    • Calendar shows the current month by default, but allow navigation to past months.
    • Total number of irrigated days (confirmed green) is calculated and displayed at the top.
    • Make sure red, blue, and light blue dots are visually distinct and accessible.

    💧 Water Budget Card Modal (Total Water Use)

    Objective:

    Allow users to explore historical total water usage (outflows) across a full calendar year, compare usage by pump, switch between monthly and cumulative trends, and optionally compare multiple years.

    📆 Access & Activation

    • Clicking on the “Total Water Use / Budget” card on the dashboard opens a modal containing a full-year line chart.
    • The default view shows the current year, broken down by month.

    📈 Graph Design & Display

    • X-axis: Month of the year (Jan–Dec)
    • Y-axis: Total water usage (in m³)
    • Tooltip on Hover: Display total usage for the selected month + breakdown by pump (if multiple are selected).
    • Graph type:
      • Line graph (one or more lines depending on selected years/pumps)

    🔧 Filter Controls

    Year Selector

    • Dropdown to select year(s) for comparison.
    • Allow multi-year comparison: overlay multiple lines for different years (e.g., 2024 vs 2025).

    Outflow (Pump) Selector

    • Multi-select checkboxes: Pump 1, Pump 2, Pump 3
    • Users can toggle any combination of pumps to isolate usage by source.

    View Type

    • Monthly (default): Each point shows usage for that month only.
    • Cumulative: Each point shows running total from Jan to that month (e.g., Feb = Jan + Feb total).

    🧠 Developer Notes

    • The data source should be consistent with water outflow logs (manual + connected meters).
    • Display unit: m³
    • Ensure graphs are responsive and color-coded for multi-year comparison.
    • Label each line clearly when multi-year comparison is active (e.g., “2024”, “2025”).
    • Cumulative logic: keep running sum for each month per selected year and pump combination.

    🌦️ ET & Rainfall Card Modals

    Objective:

    Allow users to view detailed historical data for Evapotranspiration (ET) and Rainfall through modals launched from the Water Insight dashboard. Charts should support different timeframes and display either daily or cumulative values.

    📌 Modal Access

    • Clicking on the ET or Rainfall card opens a dedicated modal.
    • Each modal contains a visual graph and time filters.

    📈 Graph filters for both ET and Rainfall

    • Time Filters (Range):
      • Last 7 days (default)
      • Last 30 days
      • Last 90 days
      • Custom (date picker)
    • View Options (Type):
      • Daily → Each point/bar represents individual day value.
      • Cumulative → Each point shows the running total.
    • Tooltip on hover:
      • Show date + value (mm)
      • For ET: also show Adjusted ET if applicable (only in ET graph)
    • Graph type: Line or bar chart (whichever fits design system)

    🌡️ ET Modal (Evapotranspiration)

    • Data to display:
      • ET₀ (reference value from weather station)
      • Adjusted ET (ET₀ × correction factor)
    • If correction factor ≠ 100%, display both ET₀ and Adjusted ET in the tooltip and legend.
    • Unit: mm per day

    🌧️ Rainfall Modal

    • Data to display:
      • Daily rainfall
      • Rainfall forecast (if available)
    • Only show actual rainfall data for now (no forecast needed at this stage).
    • Unit: mm per day

    🔧 Developer Notes

    • Graph must update dynamically when users change:
      • Date range
      • View type (daily/cumulative)
    • Default State:
      • ET modal: Show last 7 days, daily view
      • Rainfall modal: Show last 7 days, daily view

    ⚙️ Water Settings Configuration Panel (Click to expand)

    Objective:

    Allow users to set irrigation-related preferences such as water allowance, irrigation period, correction factor, and app notifications. These settings control how data is calculated and displayed across the Water Insight dashboard.

    🧾 Fields & Functional Requirements

    Annual Water Allowance (Target)

    • Users can enter a target water usage amount for the year (e.g., 75,000 m³).
    • This target is set per outflow/pump level, not tenant-wise.
    • Value is used in the Water Budget card to calculate progress and % used.
      • Note: The total water budget card is the sum of all outflow allowances.

    Irrigation Period (From / To)

    • Users define the active irrigation period during the year (e.g., March to November). This period:
      • Controls when daily irrigation notifications are triggered.
      • Filters data in ET, rainfall, days watered dashboards.
    • ⚠️ If the user changes the period mid-season (May to November), the system:
      • Preserves historical logs from outside the new date range.
      • Shows a warning: “Some data exists outside the selected irrigation period.”

    Default Irrigation Frequency

    • Drop-down to select how often irrigation typically happens:
      • Daily
      • Every other day
      • Once per week (select day)
      • Specific weekdays (multi-select: e.g., Mon, Wed, Fri)

    Mobile App Notifications

    • Toggle: Enabled / Disabled
    • If Enabled:
      • Sends daily push prompt to mobile app:
      • "Did you irrigate yesterday evening?"
      • (User can answer Yes ✅ or No ❌).
    • Default is Enabled on first setup.

    Target ET / ET Correction Factor (%)

    • A numeric field (default = 100%) that lets users adjust the ET used in calculations.
    • How it works:
      • Reference ET₀ comes from a weather station (e.g., 5.2 mm).
      • If Correction Factor = 85%, then Adjusted ET = 5.2 × 0.85 = 4.4 mm.
    • Display Logic:
      • If value ≠ 100%, both ET₀ and Adjusted ET must be shown in:
        • Insight Cards
        • ET Modals / Graphs

    Default Values that should load for the water settings per outflow

    • ET factor = 1 (100%) (no adjustment).
    • Mobile App notifications = Enabled. - Add field for “Preferred reminder time”. Default = 3 pm site-local time (important for multi-country tenants).
    • Annual Allowance = 0 (neutral until set).
    • Irrigation Period = Jan–Dec (neutral default, as periods differ worldwide).
    • Irrigation Frequency = Weekly (default = Wednesday, to avoid overwhelming with daily prompts).

    🔌 :Connected Water Meter Integration (Shayp v1.0) (Click to expand)

    Objective:

    Integrate IoT-connected water meters into the Water Insight system to capture hourly/daily flow data, display usage summaries, and distinguish between manual and automated sources.

    💼 Key Functionalities

    Device Linking (Backend Only)

    • Device linking will be handled internally by our development team (no UI at this stage).
    • Devices will be mapped in the backend via database or config setup.
    • For now, coordinate with (Sasitha, Tharuka) for device setup and data structure alignment.

    Data Storage – New Table

    • Create a new database table to store hourly inflow/outflow readings from Shayp devices.
    • Table structure should support:
      • Device ID / Source
      • Timestamp
      • Flow Direction (Inflow / Outflow)
      • Volume (m³)

    Daily Totals Calculation

    • The system should automatically compute daily totals based on the hourly inflow/outflow records.
    • These totals will be displayed in the Water Insight card.

    Toggle: Hourly / Daily / Cumulative View

    • Add a radio button toggle in the UI (total usage section or modal) with 3 options:
      • Hourly
      • Daily
      • Cumulative
    • When users switch between these views:
      • The corresponding graph or data table should update accordingly.
      • Use consistent units (m³) and color schemes for all views.

    Source Indicator (Manual vs. Automated)

    • Clearly show whether a reading is:
      • Manual (entered by user)
      • Automated (from IoT device)
    • Even if a site has connected meters, some readings may still be manual (e.g., if a specific source isn't linked to a device yet).

    📋 :Bottom Section - Water Usage Records Table (Click to expand)

    ‼️ :Wireframe here is not perfectly filled, PLEASE make sure to consider description

    Objective:

    Provide users with a detailed, filterable table of water usage entries—both manual and from connected meters—to view, edit, or delete records as needed.

    Water Records Table

    Main Features

    Tabs

    • Two tabs to switch between:
      • Manual Readings (entered by user)
      • Connected Meter Logs (auto-synced device data)

    Table Columns

    • Date → The date of the recorded usage
    • Water Flow → Pump name (e.g., Pump 1, Pump 2)
    • Measurement → Value + unit (e.g., 50500 m³)
      • Show an icon indicating source:
        • 💧 = daily consumption
        • 📟 = meter readings
    • Comments → Optional user-entered notes (e.g., “Strong drought”, “Tournament mid-day watering”)
    • Action Buttons:
      • ✏️ Edit → Opens editable popup.
      • 🗑️ Delete → Confirms deletion before removing the entry

    Filtering & Search (Standardized)

    Include Standard filters/search above the table using Simon’s new standard UI components,with filters for:

    • Date range
    • Pump name
    • Reading type (daily consumption/ meter reading)

    Pagination

    • Add standard pagination controls at the bottom of the table (e.g., 1 / 2 / 3).
    • Default to showing 10 records per page.

    ✅ Acceptance Criteria

    • ✅ Users can log water manually or via notifications
    • ✅ Insight cards display real-time values and trends with correct colour coding
    • ✅ Each card opens a modal with detailed visualisation and filters
    • ✅ Settings are configurable and dynamically update the cards
    • ✅ If correction factor is not 100%, ET card and modal show ET0 and Adjusted ET
    • ✅ Connected water meter data is displayed in hourly/daily views and separated from manual logs
    • ✅ Historical irrigation logs preserved even if irrigation period is changed, with warning message

        Card Modals

        Question 1

        When we select "Last 14 days" in the Range and "Monthly" in the Type, what exactly should the graph show?

        Question 2 - graph filters

        From what I understand,

        Range (Time Frame)

        • The selected time range (e.g., Last 14 days, 30 days, 90 days, or Custom) determines how many bars will appear.
        • For example:
          • If you choose “Last 14 days,” you’ll see 14 bars, one per day.
          • If you choose “Last 30 days,” there will be 30 bars.
          • If you choose “90 days,” there will be 90 bars, etc.

        Type

        • Monthly: Each bar represents the water usage in a single day, grouped by source (Pump 1, Pump 2, etc.).
          • Multi-select of pumps means stacked bars with colored segments per pump.
        • Cumulative: Each bar represents the running total up to that day (e.g., Day 1 = 100, Day 2 = 230, Day 3 = 400, etc.).

        If Water Meter Is Connected

        • An additional type: Hourly becomes available.
          • Then each bar will represent one hour of water usage (instead of per day).
          • By default, it will show the last 3 days worth of hourly data.

        Is this the expected behavior?

        Question 1

        Why do we still need to show this message ("Did you irrigate yesterday?") if the system already records meter readings or daily consumption?

        For example, if the message is shown but the user doesn’t click Yes or No, and instead they go and add a reading or consumption value, the message will still stay — even though the system already has the data.

        Especially for connected meters like Shayp, the readings are automatically tracked. So it feels like double work to ask the user to respond to the message after they’ve already entered the data.

        Wouldn’t it make more sense to only show the message if:

        @MadushanMaya

        • Bear in mind some cards are not site specific but overall (eg: ET, Site conditions should also for all sites etc).

        • However @MadushanMaya you make a good point: "did you irrigate yesterday" should consider outflow level.

        Proposed adjustment:

        • Keep the daily card
        • Each day shows a card: “Did you irrigate yesterday?”
        • User clicks ✅ (yes) or ❌ (no).

        NEW STEP: Inline expansion (no modal)

        • If the user clicks ✅, the card expands inline (in place).
        • It shows a list of all outflows/zones.
        • By default: all outflows are pre-ticked. IFF ONLY ONE OUTFLOWS THEN IGNORE THESE STEPS
        • User can untick zones if irrigation did not happen there.

        Memory of last choice

        • The system remembers the last configuration of ticked/unticked zones.
        • Next time, the UI pre-fills based on that.
        • Always include an “All outflows” toggle to quickly select everything again.

        Bulk confirmation

        • Allow user to select multiple day cards (e.g., tick boxes on the left of each day).
        • With one action, confirm irrigation for several days in a row.
        • Bulk confirmation uses the same remembered outflow settings, unless user expands to adjust.

        Minimal click is key

        • ✅ click should not open a modal or move the cursor elsewhere --> "inline modal "
        • The flow should support the most common case (all outflows irrigated) in 1 click.

        @HelaniJ @MadushanMaya

        I have taken the time to consider and review all your questions. Please find clarifications point by point below. If anything is still unclear, let me know — but this should give us a solid, final framework to move forward.

        1. Settings Page

        We need to refine the scope of settings as follows:

        • Site-level (global):

          • ET Factor
          • Mobile App notifications

        • Per Outflow (zone/pump level):

          • Annual allowance (water rights are often zone-specific). - Note: The total water budget card is the sum of all outflow allowances.
          • Irrigation period (different grass types or soils may require different active windows).
          • Default irrigation frequency (greens daily, fairways 2×/week, rough weekly, etc.).

        2. Default Values

        • ET factor = 1 (100%) (no adjustment).
        • Mobile App notifications = Enabled. - Add field for “Preferred reminder time”. Default = 3 pm site-local time (important for multi-country tenants).
        • Annual Allowance = 0 (neutral until set).
        • Irrigation Period = Jan–Dec (neutral default, as periods differ worldwide).
        • Irrigation Frequency = Weekly (default = Wednesday, to avoid overwhelming with daily prompts).

        3. Left-hand Section: “Did you irrigate yesterday?”

        Clarification as I believe this remains a point of concerns:

        • Context: This feature is designed to make irrigation logging frictionless while still giving us essential data.

        • Functional logic:

          • Prompts follow the frequency set in Outflow Settings.
            • Example: Frequency = Tue/Thu → prompt appears only on those days.
            • Example: Frequency = Every other day → prompt appears only on alternate days, starting from the start date field (see below).

        • Connected outflow (metered):

          • Still requires a frequency setting (valuable metadata), but no daily prompts (system knows from meter data).

        • Manual log suppression:

          • If the user logs any irrigation (at least one outflow) manually on a day → that day is automatically marked as irrigated, and the prompt is suppressed. => This is treated as the truth for that day.

        • Inline confirmation (when prompt = Yes):

          • Show outflow(s) preselected.
          • Suggest last recorded volume (manual mode).
            • If in meter mode, suggest the new meter reading as: last reading + last recorded delta.
            • Example: Last reading = 50,850; last delta = 380 → Suggest 51,230 (≈ +380 m³).
            • Guardrail: if last reading is stale (>14 days old), suggest only the delta (leave reading blank).
            • ! Important: Entry of quantities is optional (not blocking).

        • Inline flow applies to both Web and Mobile push notifications.

        4. Prompt Persistence & Calendar

        • Prompts stay open for 7 days (rolling window).
        • After 7 days, unanswered prompts are closed as “unknown/skipped”, but a record is kept in DB.
        • The Days Watered Calendar allows users to backfill or correct history (no change, just clarifying):
          • Blue = Irrigated
          • Red = No irrigation
          • Empty = Unknown
          • Light blue = Planned irrigation (future or past plan not yet confirmed)
        • Calendar click cycle (explicit):
          • Empty → Blue (irrigated) → Red (no irrigation) → Empty.
          • Outflow picker must be visible in the modal for clarity when multiple zones exist.

        5. Every Other Day Logic

        • User must select a start date when choosing “Every other day.”
        • Default start date = today (if within irrigation period) or first day of irrigation period.
        • If they later change the start date, this only affects future planned days.
        • Past data is never rewritten; history remains as originally logged.

        This rule applies to any frequency change: changes apply from tomorrow onwards only.

        One Outflow Case If only one outflow exists, no picker is shown. That single outflow is the source of truth.

        I believe this clarifies all points. Let me know if that would not be the case.

        FYI @sasitha2 @Theekshana93

        ⚙️ Settings Page

        1️⃣ Site-Level or Tenant-Level?

        Right now, you mentioned "site-level (global)".
        Do you actually mean the tenant level?

        2️⃣ Setting the Yearly Water Allowance

        👉 @godinv mentioned:

        • Annual allowance (water rights are often zone-specific)
        • Water rights are usually specific to each zone

        ℹ️ Note: We use the word zone to mean an area, like: Bunkers Greens Fairways

        If we record the yearly water allowance for each zone (area), it may cause problems.

        Why?

        • One outflow (pump) can serve many sites.
        • One site can have many zones.

        👉 This means we’d have to do reverse calculations, which can get complicated.

        A simpler approach

        • Set the yearly allowance at the outflow level instead.
        • If needed, allow the user to create a separate outflow for a specific zone inside a site.

        3️⃣ Are We Handling Grass Types Now or Later?

        👉 @godinv mentioned:
        The watering schedule may change depending on the type of grass or soil,
        since each needs water at different times.

        Should we be solving this in the current epic?

        • Once Epic 267 – Grass Species Integration is complete,
          we can add this in the next step.

        @godinv

        Could you please take a moment to review the finalized requirements under the epic description sections:

        • 🔔 Top Left section – Daily Irrigation Notification and Logging
        • 📅 Days Watered Card Modal (Irrigation Events Calendar)

        At the moment, there are a few conflicts between these two sections. It’s important that we align on how to handle them before we begin implementing the notification functionality. Anyways we’ll need to revise the calendar behavior again for the V2 release (January). (because this is supposed to act based on the notification responses)

        For now, in the V1 release (December), the calendar will behave as follows:

        • If irrigation is planned from the settings → show as light blue
        • If at least one outflow has an irrigation record → show as dark blue
        • If there are no records → show as red
        • Outflow filtering will be available
        • However, clickable day-color changes (changing irrigation state) will not be included yet

        🔍 Here are the key concerns.

        Point 1 – Data mismatch between notifications and actual records

        If a user clicks "Yes" on the "Did you irrigate yesterday?" notification but doesn't add any actual records (since it’s optional), this may cause inconsistencies between the notification response and the data shown in the calendar.

        Point 2 – Connected meters won’t receive notifications

        As agreed, we will not send notifications for connected meters.

        However, if the outflow is using manual readings or daily consumption, then notifications will be sent for those outflows.

        Point 3 – Only one outflow needs a record to remove the notification

        Let’s say a user has two outflows scheduled for that day (both manual). If they enter a record for just one of them, the system will treat the day as irrigated and won’t send a notification, even though the second outflow has no data.

        Point 4 – Meter reading sequence issue

        Notifications are kept open for 7 days.

        • Day 7 notification - outflow 1 reading 1000
        • Day 6 notification - outflow 1 reading 900
        • Day 5 notification - outflow 1 reading 800
        • Day 4 notification - outflow 1 reading 700
        • Day 3 notification - outflow 1 reading 600
        • Day 2 notification - outflow 1 reading 500
        • Day 1 notification - outflow 1 reading 400

        Now, imagine this situation:

        • Day 7: User enters a meter reading of 1000
        • Days 6 to 1: No data entered yet
        • Later, the user returns to add data for Day 6, but since they already entered 1000 for Day 7, they can’t enter a lower value (like 900 or 800) — because meter readings must increase over time.

        This isn’t a problem for daily consumption values, but for meter readings, it can block the user from entering data.

        Could you please take some time and come up with your thoughts to handle this kind of situation?

        @godinv

        Handling notification messages and manual entries:

        • If a user adds a record manually from the Water Usage table for a specific outflow, we don’t send a notification for that outflow.
        • Also, if a notification is already sent but the user manually enters a record from the table (without clicking "Yes" in the notification), the system will automatically remove the message — since the manual record confirms irrigation.

        Now, regarding the Calendar View behavior:

        On a planned irrigation day, if there is already an irrigation record saved for a specific outflow, users should not be allowed to change the irrigation status from the calendar. This is where inconsistencies can occur.

        That’s why I’m suggesting we use four color-coded statuses on the calendar to better handle this logic:

        • 🟣 Purple → Irrigation confirmed through a manual entry.
        • 🔵 Blue → Irrigation confirmed via notification, but no actual water record added.
        • 🔴 Red → “No irrigation” confirmed via notification.
        • 🔷 Light Blue → Planned irrigation based on the schedule set in Water Settings.

        This way, we can control when users are allowed to change status colors — only when there are no actual records for that day. If there's an actual reading, the system should lock the status and prevent changes to avoid confusion.

        Currently, even if we add a warning like "Irrigation declared, but no amount confirmed", the system still allows users to change the status (e.g., from blue to red or light blue), even though there is real recorded data.

        @godinv Could you please confirm on this approach?

        @godinv

        Notification section - newest requirement and how it should work together with bulk confirmation.

        Based on the current logic, we always suggest the next meter reading using the last saved reading plus the last delta (water usage).

        However, in bulk confirmation, the user may select several notifications for the same meter‑reading outflow, but on different days.

        Example:

        • Friday – Outflow 1
        • Wednesday – Outflow 1
        • Monday – Outflow 1

        If the last saved reading in the backend is 50,850, then the only suggestion we can reliably generate is something like 51,230 (based on the previous data).

        But we cannot automatically suggest different readings for different days in the bulk selection, because we only know the latest reading. We can only suggest one single next reading based on the last stored value.

        So the question is:

        How should we handle suggestions when multiple days are selected in bulk confirmation for the same meter outflow?

        Could you please confirm how you want us to handle this scenario.

        For mobile push notifications, I’d like to suggest the following approach.

        A separate notification is sent for each outflow that had irrigation planned (based on Outflow Settings).

        🧾 Notification Message Format

        •   The message shows:
          •   Date (e.g., “Monday, 23rd June 2025”)
          •   Text: “Did you irrigate yesterday from Outflow 1?”
        •   Two action buttons:
          •   ✅ Yes
          •   ❌ No
        •   These buttons appear directly on the lock screen or notification tray, so users can respond without opening the app.

        ⚠️ However, when a user taps “Yes”, it’s not ideal to open an inline expansion from the lock screen to get irrigation values. This would require calling open APIs, which could raise security and privacy concerns.

        ✅ Instead, when the user taps “Yes”, the app will open a notification panel inside the mobile app. This panel will display all pending irrigation prompts, where users can enter water values for each outflow and confirm. (We won't keep 7 days' history on this, if the user clicks on a notification on 18-11-2025 all the outflows will be listed on that day).

        👉 Entering water usage is optional — not required.

        In the future, we can expand this notification panel to include other types of push notifications as well.

        Would this approach work for you? Happy to adjust based on your input.

        Create new emoji

        Hi @godinv, @HelaniJ,

        After going through your conversation, I noticed a few user-experience issues and technical issues.
        Below is my proposed solution for the notification section, broken down into Web and Mobile.

        1. Web Application

        How Notifications Work

        • Users receive notifications based on the settings configured for each outflow.

        • The notification list shows all notifications generated within the past 7 days.

        User Actions

        • Users can:

          • Select multiple or all notifications and mark Yes or No without entering any values.

          • Enter values only by expanding a single notification.
            (👉 Multi-selection is not allowed when entering values.)

        When User Expands a Notification

        1. If there are no irrigation records in the DB for later dates:

          • Prefill the input field with the last submitted consumption value for that outflow.

          • When the user taps Save, show a confirmation prompt to prevent accidental submissions.

        2. If there are irrigation records after that date:

          • The input field remains empty.

          • Display min/max allowed values based on surrounding records to guide user validation.

        2. Mobile Application

        The current proposed wireframes raise several UX and technical concerns.
        Below is an improved approach.

        How Notifications Work on Mobile

        • Users receive push notifications based on the outflow settings.

        • If a notification is submitted on the web app, OR it is older than 7 days,
          → It should also be cleared from the mobile notification tray.

        Behavior in Notification Tray

        • Tap "No"

          • The system immediately records the response as No, without opening the app.
            (Note: As discussed with @Charith-Wije, this requires an additional push-notification handler.
            FYI @sasitha2, @Theekshana93)

        • Tap "Yes" OR tap the notification itself

          • The mobile app opens and navigates to a screen showing all notifications for that day.

          • Users can:

            • Select multiple or all notifications and submit Yes/No (same as web).

            • Enter values for individual outflows by expanding each item (same as web).

        Additional Mobile Navigation

        • The mobile app will include a dedicated Notification section.

        • Users can view all valid irrigation notifications by date.

        • Tapping an irrigation notification for a specific date takes them to that day's irrigation notifications (same flow as above).

        Edited 3 months ago by Madushan Lamahewa

      • Helani Jayawardena @HelaniJ 2 months ago
        Create new emoji

        @godinv

        Based on our latest agreement, when a user selects multiple days for the same outflow, and enters a single meter reading, we divide the difference evenly across those selected days.


        For example:


        If the user selects Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday for Outflow 1 and enters a value of 150, the system will save 50 for each day.

        But let’s consider a more complex scenario:

        • Monday – Outflow 1 (value: 1000)
        • Tuesday – Outflow 1
        • Wednesday – Outflow 1
        • Thursday – Outflow 1 (value: 900)
        • Friday – Outflow 1
        • Saturday – Outflow 1 (value: 800)

        If the user selects Tuesday, Wednesday, and Friday for bulk confirmation, we face a problem.
        Although there are 3 selected days, the reading on Monday (1000) limits the maximum reading we can save for Wednesday and Tuesday.

        So if the user enters 980, we calculate:


        980 - 800 = 180 → divide by 3 = 60 per day.


        That would result in saving:

        • Friday: 860 ✅
        • Wednesday: 960 ❌ (Partially oky)
        • Tuesday: 1020 ❌ (Also not valid, as it breaks the sequence from Monday)

        ⚠️ Because of this, the total reading split won’t be valid in this case.

        Suggestion:


        To avoid such issues, we propose not allowing users to multi-select days if there are already saved readings in between the selected dates for that outflow.

        Would you agree with this approach?

      • Helani Jayawardena @HelaniJ 2 months ago
        Create new emoji

        @godinv They are water meter readings. My concern is about the bulk confirmation logic we agreed on.

        For example, if the notifications are as given below:

        • Monday – Outflow 1
        • Tuesday – Outflow 2
        • Wednesday – Outflow 1
        • Thursday – Outflow 2
        • Friday – Outflow 1

        Then we will show only two input fields:

        • one for Outflow 1 and one for Outflow 2.

        After the user enters the values, we divide the Outflow 1 value by 3 days and the Outflow 2 value by 2 days, and save the readings.

        In the earlier example, the meter reading was 980.
        So for Outflow 1, we divide 180 units by 3 and get 60 units per day.

        But the issue is that we cannot fit two days * 60 units between Thursday and Monday because the gap between those readings is only 100 units.
        So the calculated values do not match the actual meter gap.

        I hope this explanation makes my concern clearer.

      • Helani Jayawardena @HelaniJ 1 month ago
        Create new emoji

        @godinv This issue has now been resolved.

        Using our example:

        • Monday – Outflow 1 (value: 1000)
        • Tuesday – Outflow 1
        • Wednesday – Outflow 1
        • Thursday – Outflow 1 (value: 900)
        • Friday – Outflow 1
        • Saturday – Outflow 1 (value: 800)

        If the user selects Tuesday, Wednesday, and Friday together, the system will split the input into two separate sections (blocks) based on the existing readings in between.

        Each block will:

        • Allow the user to enter a value
        • Show the valid meter reading range for that block, based on the surrounding readings

        This approach avoids invalid calculations and keeps the meter readings consistent.

        We are still fine‑tuning the wireframes, but the logic will follow this approach.
